steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: IUPAC: longest chain, number for lowest locants, prefixes for substituents, suffix for functional group

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Mechanisms: curly arrows show electron pair movement; SN1: carbocation intermediate (3 deg > 2 deg > 1 deg ); SN2: concerted backside attack (1 deg favoured)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Markovnikov: H adds to carbon with more H's (forms more stable carbocation)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Oxidation: 1 deg alcohol -> aldehyde -> carboxylic acid; 2 deg -> ketone; 3 deg resistant

steps.title: Worked example
steps.body: Q: Propose a mechanism for the reaction of 2-methylpropene with HBr --- Solution: Electrophilic addition. H⁺ adds to less substituted C (Markovnikov) -> more stable 3 deg carbocation (CH₃)₃C⁺. Br⁻ attacks carbocation -> 2-bromo-2-methylpropane. Curly arrows: pi bond to H, H-Br bond to Br

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Name: CH₃CH₂CH(OH)CH₃ | Mechanism for SN2 hydrolysis of CH₃CH₂Br with OH⁻ | Product of oxidation of CH₃CH₂CH₂OH with acidified K₂Cr₂O₇

steps.title: Lesson plan
steps.body: Starter (5 min): Recall prior knowledge of organic chemistry with quick questions. Teaching (15 min): Work through each of the learning objectives, explaining principles step by step. Key points review (5 min): Revisit the key points together, confirming understanding. Worked example (10 min): Model the example question: Propose a mechanism for the reaction of 2-methylpropene with HBr. Solution: Electrophilic addition. H⁺ adds to less substituted C (Markovnikov) -> more stable 3 deg carbocation (CH₃)₃C⁺. Br⁻ attacks carbocation -> 2-bromo-2-methylpropane. Curly arrows: pi bond to H, H-Br bond to Br Practice (10 min): Students attempt the practice questions independently; circulate and support. Plenary (5 min): Review answers and address misconceptions.
